chunks: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to perform the Hajj and to bring Ismail with him to perform it, and to settle him in the Sacred Precincts. So they performed the Hajj on a red camel, with none accompanying them except Jibra'il (peace be upon him). When they reached the Sacred Precincts, Jibra'il said to him: 'O Ibrahim, dismount and perform the ritual bath before

They both entered the Sacred Sanctuary and dismounted, then performed the ritual bath. Jibra'il showed them how to prepare for the ihram, and they did so. Then he commanded them to enter into ihram for the Hajj and instructed them in the four talbiyahs with which the Messengers had made the proclamation. Then he led them to al-Safa where they stopped. Jibra'il stood between them, faced the House, and proclaimed Allahu Akbar — and they both did likewise. He said 'La ilaha illa Allah' — they followed. He praised Allah and they praised. He glorified and they glorified. He exalted Allah, and they did the same. Jibra'il advanced and they advanced with him, praising and glorifying Allah the Mighty and Majestic, until he brought them to the Black Stone. Jibra'il reverently touched the Stone and commanded them both to do likewise. He then led them in seven circuits of circumambulation, then stood with them at the station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and prayed two rak'ahs — and they both prayed. He then showed them all the rites and what they should do. When they had completed their rites, Allah commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to depart. Isma'il remained alone, with no one but his mother.

In the following year, Allah gave Ibrahim (peace be upon him) permission for the Hajj and the building of the Ka'ba. The Arabs had been performing pilgrimage to it, though it was only a heap of rubble — its foundations were still recognizable. When the people departed, Isma'il gathered the stones and placed them inside the Ka'ba. When Allah granted them permission for the construction, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) arrived and said: 'O my son, Allah has commanded us to build the Ka'ba.' They cleared it and found a single red stone. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'Place its foundation upon it.' Allah sent down four angels to gather the stones for him. Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both) laid the stones while the angels handed them stones, until it reached a height of twelve cubits. They prepared two doors for it: one to enter through and one to exit through. They set thresholds and iron hinges on the doors. The Ka'ba stood bare and uncovered. Ibrahim departed having completed and levelled the House, while Isma'il remained. When the people came to him...

When the people came, Isma'il saw a woman from the tribe of Himyar whose beauty struck him, and he asked Allah the Mighty and Majestic to give her to him in marriage. She had a husband, so Allah decreed death upon her husband. She remained in Mecca in grief over her husband, but Allah removed that grief from her and gave her in marriage to Isma'il. Ibrahim came for the Hajj — she was a righteous and guided woman. Isma'il set out for al-Ta'if to fetch food for his family. She looked upon a dishevelled old man who asked her about their condition; she told him of their good state. He asked her specifically about Isma'il, and she told him of his excellent character. He asked her where she was from, and she said: 'A woman of Himyar.' Ibrahim departed without meeting Isma'il, but he had written a letter. He said: 'Hand this to your husband when he comes, if Allah wills.' Isma'il returned to her and she handed him the letter. He read it and said: 'Do you know who that old man was?' She said: 'I saw him — a handsome man with a resemblance to you.' He said: 'That was Ibrahim.' She exclaimed: 'Alas, what shame before him!' He said: 'Why? Did he look at something of your charms?' She said: 'No, but I feared I may have been remiss in my duties.' The wise woman said to him: 'Would you not hang on these two doors two curtains — a curtain from this side and...'

A curtain from this side. He said to her: 'Yes.' So they both made twelve-cubit curtains and hung them on the two doors. They were both delighted with that. She said: 'Would I not also weave garments for the Ka'ba to cover it entirely? For these stones are unsightly.' Isma'il said to her: 'Certainly.' She hastened to do this and sent to her people a great quantity of wool, asking them to spin it. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, from that arose the custom of women asking one another to spin, for that very reason.' He said: She hastened and sought help in the work, and whenever she completed a panel she would hang it up. The Hajj season came but one side of the Ka'ba remained uncovered. She said to Isma'il: 'What shall we do with this side that the kiswa did not reach?' So they covered it with palm-leaf matting. The Hajj season came and the Arabs came to it as they customarily did. They saw something that delighted them and said: 'It is fitting that the caretaker of this House be given gifts.' From then on, the practice of hadiy (sacrificial offerings) arose. Every clan of the Arabs brought something to carry — silver and other things — until a great amount had accumulated. So they removed that palm-leaf matting...

They completed the covering (kiswa) of the House and hung two doors on it. The Ka'ba had not been roofed, so Isma'il placed in it wooden columns like the ones you see today, and Isma'il roofed it with palm fronds, then levelled it with clay. The Arabs came the following year, entered the Ka'ba, saw its construction, and said: 'The caretaker of this House deserves additional reward.' When the following year came, the hadiy came to him, but Isma'il did not know what to do with it. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'Slaughter it and feed it to the pilgrims.' He (the Imam) said: Isma'il complained to Ibrahim about the scarcity of water. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to Ibrahim: 'Dig a well that will provide drink for the pilgrims.' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended and dug their well — meaning Zamzam — until its water appeared. Then Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: 'Come down, O Ibrahim.' He descended after Jibra'il and said: 'O Ibrahim, strike the four corners of the well and say: In the name of Allah.' He said: So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) struck the corner adjacent to...

the House, saying 'Bismillah,' and a spring burst forth. Then he struck the second corner saying 'Bismillah,' and a spring burst forth. Then he struck the third, saying 'Bismillah,' and a spring burst forth. Then he struck the fourth, saying 'Bismillah,' and a spring burst forth. Jibra'il said to him: 'Drink, O Ibrahim, and supplicate for your offspring in it with blessing.' Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Jibra'il came out of the well together, and Jibra'il said to him: 'Pour water upon yourself, O Ibrahim, and circumambulate the House, for this is a provision of water with which Allah shall water the children of Ismail.' So Ibrahim departed and Ismail accompanied him until he exited the Sacred Precincts. Ibrahim went on his way, and Ismail returned to the Sacred Precincts.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَاتُ الْأَرْبَعُ: The four talbiyahs -- the formulaic declarations (labbayk) recited by prophets upon entering Hajj
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: Ihram -- the state of ritual consecration entered upon beginning Hajj or Umra, requiring specific dress and behavior
key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) -- touched by Jibra'il and then by Ibrahim and Ismail
key_terms.الْكِسْوَةُ: The kiswa -- the cloth covering of the Ka'ba; this hadith presents the first kiswa woven by Ismail's wife
key_terms.الْمَقَامُ: Maqam Ibrahim -- the Standing Place of Ibrahim, site of prayer after tawaf
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكُ: The rites of Hajj -- the full sequence of ritual acts performed during pilgrimage
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: Hadiy -- the sacrificial animal offered during Hajj; this narration gives its historical origin
key_terms.زَمْزَمُ: Zamzam -- the sacred well in Makkah, dug here by Jibra'il at divine command for the Hajj pilgrims

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of Hajj rituals according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the foundational account of how God commanded Ibrahim (AS) to perform the first Hajj with his son Ismail (AS), guided by the angel Jibra'il. The hadith details the origin of key Hajj rituals -- ghusl before entering ihram, the talbiyah, circumambulation, the prayer at Maqam Ibrahim, and the touching of the Black Stone -- all instituted under divine and angelic instruction. It then recounts the building of the Ka'ba, the institution of the kiswa (the covering of the Ka'ba), the origin of the hadiy (sacrificial offering), the roofing of the Ka'ba, and finally the miraculous digging of Zamzam under the guidance of Jibra'il. This narrative would have been understood by early Muslims as establishing the prophetic precedent and divine origin of all Hajj rites performed to this day.
